newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down as mkt braces for Negara intervention.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down as mkt braces for Negara intervention.

text.p: * Market sells down ringgit, but braces for Bank Negara's intervention at 2.5250
* Ringgit's gains late on Friday due to Bank Negara's presence, say dealers
* Selling of ringgit prompted by slight weakening of Malaysian interbank money rates
* Chartists say dollar/ringgit poised to break 2.5250/60, this year's high

The ringgit continued to be sold down on Monday morning by big offshore players, but more cautiously on fear that there may be a fresh intervention by Bank Negara Malaysia around 2.5250 a dollar, dealers said.
They said Bank Negara intervened on Friday to sell around $100 million to support the ringgit at 2.5250 a dollar after a heavy attack on the local currency.
No confirmation was available from Bank Negara, which does not comment on its open market intervention.
"The market looks poised to test 2.5250 again," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said the intervention on Friday brought dollar/ringgit down to 2.5220 by Monday morning, but not for long. It retreated soon after on technical and speculative selling pressure.
"The selling is probably because of the fall in interbank rates in Malaysia. The one month has dipped quite a bit and Bank Negara is seen focusing on interbank rates," a dealer said.
"This is sending mixed signals to people," he added.
An analyst with a Singapore-based research house said the volumes on Friday suggest the intervention was not very big.
"It could have been a central bank bluff. People will test the level againt to see if Bank Negara is really in," he said.
At 0235 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5233/43 to a dollar.
